high.title: Taiwan Stock Market: NT$650 Billion Dividend Inflow Expected in August — Quanta, CTBC Financial Among Key Drivers
high.summary:
Taiwan's listed companies are set to distribute a massive NT$650 billion in cash dividends during August 2026, providing a significant liquidity tailwind for the equity market. A total of 451 companies have scheduled August dividend payments, led by Quanta Computer (2382) at NT$60.2 billion and CTBC Financial (2891) at NT$49.1 billion, followed by Chunghwa Telecom (NT$40.3 billion), Shin Kong Financial (NT$24.8 billion), and Yuanta Financial (NT$23.9 billion). The backdrop is exceptionally strong: Taiwan-listed companies collectively recorded a historic NT$4.5 trillion in net profit in the prior fiscal year, driven by the AI demand supercycle benefiting advanced semiconductor manufacturing, packaging, PCBs, assembly, and thermal management. Total cash dividends industry-wide surged to a record NT$2.49 trillion, up nearly NT$200 billion year-over-year. **Market Implication:** The NT$650 billion August dividend wave represents a powerful reinvestment catalyst. Historically, a significant portion of dividend proceeds flows back into equities, supporting index levels during seasonal volatility. Fund managers should monitor ex-dividend reinvestment patterns across financial holding companies and AI supply chain names, as these could anchor market support heading into Q3.

high.title: [TSMC: Cathay 5C Purchase 16 — Strong Performance; Revenue Outlook Upgraded to 40%+ Growth]
high.summary:
TSMC (2330) shares rebounded strongly on July 31, reclaiming all moving average levels, closing at NT$2,425 (+NT$220). Despite Q2 financials coming in roughly in line with expectations — and market concerns over gross margin dilution from accelerated 2nm ramp — the stock found support from its reasonable P/E valuation, sustained technological leadership, and robust AI-driven demand outlook.

Key financial highlights: Q3 2026 revenue guidance of USD $44.6–$45.8 billion (midpoint ~+12% QoQ), driven by strong HPC demand and 2nm volume acceleration. Q3 gross margin guided at 65–67%, with the midpoint slightly below consensus, as 2nm ramp is expected to dilute margins by 3–4 percentage points.

Critically, TSMC upgraded its full-year 2026 USD revenue growth outlook from "above 30%" to "above 40%" — a meaningful positive revision. Capital expenditure was also raised from USD $52–56 billion to USD $60–64 billion, signaling strong conviction in future AI demand and reflecting rising construction costs.

On capacity expansion, TSMC announced an additional USD $100 billion investment in Arizona (on top of the previously announced USD $165 billion), and plans to build 13 new fabs and advanced packaging facilities in Taiwan, reaffirming Taiwan as its primary manufacturing and R&D hub.

medium.title: Liteon Technology Already Much Changed! CEO Chiu Sen-pin Uses Two Strategies for Transformation — Targeting Multiple NT$30 Billion-Scale Clients Long-Term
medium.summary: Liteon Technology (2301), traditionally a power supply unit (PSU) manufacturer, is demonstrating tangible progress in its pivot to a high-value solutions provider. President Chiu Sen-pin announced that two newly added Cloud Service Providers (CSPs) are each expected to contribute approximately USD 1 billion (roughly NT$32 billion) in annual revenue by 2028. The company currently already has two such large-scale key accounts (KAs), and management is confident in cultivating a total of 7–8 KAs at the USD 1 billion order level over the long term. Liteon's Battery Backup Unit (BBU) business — a core product of its cloud business division — is a key driver: production capacity is being ramped from 600,000 units last year to 900,000 units this year, with analysts estimating year-on-year growth of at least 70%. The strategic shift from single-component supplier to system-level supplier, including rack integration services, is seen as the critical differentiator. For fund managers, Liteon represents a meaningful transformation story among Taiwan's legacy hardware names, with North American hyperscaler exposure providing durable revenue visibility into 2028 and beyond.

medium.title: Sigurd Microelectronics Invests NT$28.5 Billion to Expand Capacity — Longtan Plant to Add Advanced Testing Equipment and Smart Production Lines
medium.summary: Sigurd Microelectronics (3264), a semiconductor testing services company, has received approval from Taiwan's Invest in Taiwan Office to invest approximately NT$28.5 billion in expanding its Longtan, Taoyuan facility. The investment will focus on advanced testing equipment and intelligent production lines, incorporating AI-assisted defect classification and packaging image recognition systems to improve yield and efficiency. Solar power generation facilities will also be installed to reduce carbon emissions. The expansion is driven by surging demand for high-end chip testing, particularly related to AI applications. This announcement is part of a broader NT$30.8 billion approval round covering four companies. For investors, Sigurd's aggressive capacity build-out positions it as a key beneficiary of the AI-driven semiconductor supply chain expansion in Taiwan, and signals continued strong demand visibility in advanced chip testing services.

medium.title: U.S. Stocks Rise but Taiwan Futures Night Session Falls Sharply — Next Week's Focus on Kai Ji Bank, Hon Hai Performance
medium.summary: U.S. major indices closed broadly higher (DJIA +0.53%, Nasdaq +1.0%, S&P 500 +0.7%), but Taiwan index futures fell over 1,000 points in the night session to 42,650, with TSMC futures dropping NT$74 to NT$2,361. Analysts attribute the overnight decline primarily to a mean-reversion correction after Taiwan's daytime session surged over 3,100 points on July 31st, with TSMC hitting the limit-up of +9.98%, a move that outpaced TSMC's ADR gains of only +0.23%. Market strategists from Taishin and Sinopac securities note that if the TAIEX can hold above the 5-day MA (41,665) and 10-day MA (42,834) on Monday, the medium-term rebound trajectory remains intact. Key stocks to watch include Kai Ji Bank (2883) and Hon Hai (2317), both of which saw coordinated buying from foreign investors, investment trusts, and proprietary dealers on July 31st. **Implication:** The night session pullback appears technical rather than fundamental; monitoring institutional flows into Hon Hai and financials will be critical for gauging Monday's open.
